title: Section 87 and the bank's alteration remark

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. A bank returns a cheque marked alteration in amount. Does that remark alone make it void under Section Eighty Seven?
scenes.shown: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. A bank returns a cheque marked "alteration in amount". Does that remark alone make it void under Section 87?

scenes.dialogue: On twenty seventh October, twenty twenty six, the Delhi High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Sanjeev Narula, answered that question.
scenes.shown: On 27 October 2026, the Delhi High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Sanjeev Narula, answered that question.

scenes.dialogue: Under a twenty thirteen collaboration agreement, the complainant was to develop the petitioner's Ghaziabad property, and get its first and second floors.
scenes.shown: Under a 2013 collaboration agreement, the complainant was to develop the petitioner's Ghaziabad property, and get its first and second floors.

scenes.dialogue: After disputes, they settled in February twenty sixteen, says the complainant. He gave up his claim to the second floor and its roof rights, for thirty lakh rupees.
scenes.shown: After disputes, they settled in February 2016, says the complainant. He gave up his claim to the second floor and its roof rights, for ₹30 lakh.

scenes.dialogue: The petitioner issued three cheques of ten lakh rupees each. Two were returned for insufficient funds; the bank returned the third, citing alteration in amount.
scenes.shown: The petitioner issued three cheques of ₹10 lakh each. Two were returned for insufficient funds; the bank returned the third, citing "alteration in amount".

scenes.dialogue: The trial court convicted him under Section One Thirty Eight, and his appeal failed. In revision, he argued the cheques were only security, and the third was void.
scenes.shown: The trial court convicted him under Section 138, and his appeal failed. In revision, he argued the cheques were only security, and the third was void.

scenes.dialogue: With signatures and delivery admitted, the High Court held the Section One Thirty Nine presumption applied, and the security defence did not rebut it.
scenes.shown: With signatures and delivery admitted, the High Court held the Section 139 presumption applied, and the security defence did not rebut it.

scenes.dialogue: On the third cheque, the amount in words and figures matched, and no change to an existing entry was proved. The bank's remark alone did not prove it void.
The conviction was upheld. So was the compensation of forty two lakh rupees. But given the property deal and deposits, the sentence was cut from ten months to six.
scenes.shown: The conviction was upheld. So was the compensation of ₹42 lakh. But given the property deal and deposits, the sentence was cut from ten months to six.
